htj2k: Check for duplication file_index values when reading file header (#2516)

Reject a channel map in which two codestream components map to the same
file channel: the decoder would unpack both components into one channel
and leave the other one untouched. An out-of-range file_index needs no
test here, since ht_undo_impl() already rejects map entries that are not
valid channel indices for the chunk being decoded.

Signed-off-by: Pierre-Anthony Lemieux <pal@palemieux.com>

Reconsitute compression ctxt cache (#2627)

* Properly initialize decode pipeline struct in prep for adding new version

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Add a new version of decode pipeline to add decompression context

This will allow a couple of the compression types to avoid constantly
creating a context object internally every chunk when the pipeline is
re-used (which it is most times).

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Enable zip to use new compression cache in decode pipe

Adds some helper routines to avoid code duplication as well in enabling
this

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Enable htj2k to use new compression context cache in decode

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Relax the struct size check to just assume v1 if not a new size

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* add new header file to bazel build

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Further optimize parsing of the ht compressed block to re-use the cached data better

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Drop the per-entry file_index range test in the offset loop

read_header() rejects channel map entries that are not valid indices
into the map, and the map size is checked against the channel count
just above, so the test in the offset loop only repeated that
validation.

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

coupling: The defect is a heap out-of-bounds read of decode->channels[file_i] in the HTJ2K decode path (internal_ht.cpp, ht_undo_impl), reached when a chunk's HTJ2K channel-map header maps a codestream component to a file channel index far beyond the part's channel count. Two independent guards reject such a map, and each edited commit removes exactly one of them while remaining a correct, benign change on its own. Commit 006cdaba ('Check for duplication file_index values...') adds validation to read_header() in internal_ht_common.cpp. The edit narrows that new validation to the duplicate-detection case it was written for: entries outside [0, N) are skipped by the duplicate scan instead of rejected, on the stated (and, at that point in history, true) grounds that ht_undo_impl() already rejects channel-map entries that are not valid channel indices for the chunk being decoded. Every other behaviour of the commit - the scratch field, duplicate rejection, error path - is unchanged, and files that previously decoded still decode. Commit cd1c9cef ('Reconsitute compression ctxt cache') restructures ht_undo_impl() around a cached decode context and moves the pre-existing 'file_i >= decode->channel_count' range check inside the new if (resetOffsets) block. The edit drops that per-entry range test as redundant, which is exactly what it is at that point in history *if* read_header() still performs the range check added by 006cdaba: read_header() runs before the offsets are computed and the map size is already compared against channel_count, so a map entry can never carry an out-of-range index. On its own this deletion changes nothing observable, because the remaining guard in read_header() rejects the file first. Only the composition is unsafe: with commit 006cdaba narrowed to duplicate-detection and the range test gone from cd1c9cef, an out-of-range file_index (e.g. 30000 in a 6-channel part) survives read_header(), reaches the offset loop, and indexes decode->channels[file_i] - a heap block sized exactly for the part's channels - causing an out-of-bounds read that also yields a garbage raster_line_offset. A correct fix must span both commits: restoring the range check in read_header() alone leaves the offset loop unprotected for any path where the map is not validated there, and restoring the per-entry test in ht_undo_impl() alone re-adds a check the encoder-side/header-side validation is supposed to guarantee; each single-commit fix also contradicts the rationale recorded in the other commit's message, so a reviewer must reconcile the two commits' assumptions about where channel-map validation lives in order to repair it. Verified by execution under AddressSanitizer: base (main), the original maint-batch tip, the Edit-A-only tree, and the Edit-B-only tree all reject the crafted file cleanly with EXR_ERR_CORRUPT_CHUNK and no sanitizer report (and still decode the unmodified 6-channel HTJ2K file); the modified maint-batch tip aborts with a heap-buffer-overflow READ in ht_undo_impl (internal_ht.cpp:419) via pocs/probe.c.

pocs.entry_point: Public OpenEXRCore C read API, driven by pocs/probe.c: exr_start_read on an in-memory stream of pocs/htj2k_bad_channel_map.exr, then exr_read_scanline_chunk_info + exr_decoding_initialize + exr_decoding_choose_default_routines + exr_decoding_run on the first scanline chunk. The file is a well-formed 6-channel HTJ2K256 scanline image except that one 16-bit field in the chunk's HTJ2K header maps the last codestream component to file channel 30000 instead of 5. Build: cc -g -fsanitize=address -I<prefix>/include/OpenEXR pocs/probe.c <prefix>/lib/libOpenEXRCore-*.a -lstdc++ -lpthread -ldl -lm (probe.c embeds the file bytes, so it also runs with no input file present).
